_comment: Round 5: the three ownership-ask variants added in v4 of policies/gdpr-dsar-copy.json (ack_claim_evidence, status_claim_evidence, late_claim_evidence; block need_claim_evidence) through the gate's own gate.py (check -> pending -> review -> check) in a scratch mirror of this tree, under the gdpr rubric as amended in the same commit (rule 2 names the ownership ask). Bodies carry example dates (received 11 November 2026, due 11 December 2026, next 26 November 2026): fixed wording, no personal data. The statements were signed with a THROWAWAY key that exists only in the scratch mirror, so none of these is a verdict the production gate accepts: the verdict a send needs is the one the reviewer host signs on the body node-8 authors after deploy. The mirror differs from the tree in one file, the allowed-signers list. One reviewer pass, 3 bodies, 3 approve.
gdpr_tree: the working tree that became the commit carrying this file

items.note: Acknowledgement states the received date and the answer date, states the one-month rule as a plain fact without naming an article, asks only for permitted proof, and says the request stays open.

Status update says the request is open, asks only for a matching link or a label/management document, names no article, states the received date and the next-contact date, no apology, no promise beyond the date.
Late status update says once that we are late and sorry, gives no reason, keeps the request open, asks only for permitted proof, and states the next date; date arithmetic is for code to confirm.
